Rashi on Megillah 26b:10:1.english: Perisa [curtain] - A cloth that is spread around the inside of the ark:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:10:2.english: It is an accessory of an accessory - [It is] an accessory of the ark:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:10:3.hebrew: דעייפי ליה - פעמים שכופלין אותו תחת ס"ת:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:10:3.english: That they fold it over - Sometimes they fold it beneath a Torah scroll:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:11:1.hebrew: דאירפט - ארון שנתקלקל ונפרד מחבורו, ויש דוגמתו בברייתא ביבמות (דף קב.): "מנעל המרופט":
Rashi on Megillah 26b:11:1.english: That has fallen apart - [Referring to] an ark that has deteriorated and separated from its joints, and there is a similar [expression] in a Baraita in Yevamot (102a): "a tattered shoe":

Rashi on Megillah 26b:11:2.english: A smaller ark - To make a small ark from the first, large one:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:11:4.english: [It is] prohibited - because it has descended from its [level of] sanctity:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:11:5.english: A curtain that has become worn out - The curtains of the ark that have become worn out:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:11:6.hebrew: לחומשין - יש ספרים שהן עשויין כל חומש לבדו, וכולן בגליון:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:11:6.english: For Chumashim - There are books that are made [with] each Chumash [book of the Torah] by itself, and all of them are [written] on parchment [scrolls]:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:12:1.english: Zevilei [cases] - Like a kind of leather bag:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:12:2.hebrew: קמטרא - ארגז שקורין אשקריניי"ו, והרבה יש בתרגום של יהונתן בן עוזיאל: "חבלים חבושים (יחזקאל כז) ארגזים" — "אמליץ דזהוריתא בקמטרין"; וכן "לאשר על המלתחה" — "לדעל קמטרי'" (מלכים ב י׳:כ״ב):
Rashi on Megillah 26b:12:2.english: Kamtera - A chest, which is called escrin [in Old French]. And there are many [instances of this word] in the Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel: "bound with cords, chests" (Ezekiel 27[:24]) [is translated] "wrapped in crimson in chests [bekamterin]"; and similarly, "to him who was over the wardrobe" (II Kings 10:22) [is translated] "to him who was over the chests [kamteraya]":

Rashi on Megillah 26b:13:1.hebrew: בי כנישתא דרומאי - אנשי ישראל באו מרומי למחוזא, ונתיישבו שם, ועשו להם בית הכנסת:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:13:1.english: A synagogue of the Romans - Jews came from Rome to Mechoza, settled there, and made themselves a synagogue:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:13:2.hebrew: אידרונא - חדר שמשימין בו מת, והיה מונח בו מת עד שלא נקבר:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:13:2.english: Idrona - A room in which they place a corpse, and a corpse was lying in it before it was buried.

Rashi on Megillah 26b:13:3.hebrew: מחית - כמו מונח, כדמתרגמינן "ותנח בגדו אצלה" — "ואחיתתיה" (בראשית ל״ט:ט״ז):
Rashi on Megillah 26b:13:3.english: [Was] lying - like "placed," as we translate [into Aramaic] "and she laid his garment beside her" (Genesis 39:16) [as] *va'acheitateih* [ואחיתתיה]:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:13:4.hebrew: בעו כהני למיעל ולצלויי - בההוא כנישתא, אין יכולין ליכנס מפני הטומאה הנכנסת בבית הכנסת דרך הפתח מבית לבית, דהכי תנן במסכת אהלות (פ"ג משנה ז):
Rashi on Megillah 26b:13:4.english: The priests wished to enter and pray - in that synagogue, [and] they could not enter because of the ritual impurity that enters into the synagogue through the opening from room to room, for so we learned in a Mishnah in Tractate Ohalot (3:7):

Rashi on Megillah 26b:13:5.english: Lift up the ark - Raise the ark from its place:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:13:6.hebrew: כלי עץ העשוי לנחת - במקום אחד, אינו מקבל טומאה, דאיתקש כלי עץ לשק לענין טומאה, דכתיב: "וכל כלי עץ או בגד או עור או שק" (ויקרא יא) — מה שק המיטלטל, אף כלי עץ המיטלטל: כל דבר המקבל טומאה, אינו חוצץ בפני הטומאה:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:13:6.english: A wooden utensil that is made to rest - in one place is not susceptible to ritual impurity, for a wooden utensil is compared to a sack with regard to ritual impurity, as it is written: "And any wooden utensil, or garment, or skin, or sack" (Leviticus 11[:32]) — just as a sack is portable, so too [only] a wooden utensil that is portable [is susceptible to impurity]: Anything that is susceptible to ritual impurity does not interpose against ritual impurity:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:15:1.hebrew: מטפחות ספרים - אף של ס"ת:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:15:1.english: Wrapping cloths of scrolls - Even [those] of a Torah scroll:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:16:1.hebrew: ואפילו שונה הלכות - כלומר, אפילו לא שימש תלמידי חכמים בהש"ס ובגמרא, אלא במשניות ובברייתות:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:16:1.english: And even [one who] studies halakhot - That is to say, even [if] he did not serve Torah scholars in the Shas [the Six Orders] and in the Gemara, but only in Mishnayot and in Baraitot:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:17:1.english: From a synagogue into a study hall - To turn a synagogue into a study hall:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:1:1.english: To drink beer with it - to buy [ingredients] with the proceeds and make beer to drink:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:2:1.hebrew: תילא - כל בית הרוס קרוי תל, כמו "והיתה תל עולם" (דברים יג):
Rashi on Megillah 26b:2:1.english: A mound [tila] - Any ruined house is called a tel [mound], as [in the verse]: "and it shall be an everlasting mound [tel olam]" (Deuteronomy 13[:17]):

Rashi on Megillah 26b:3:1.english: Beams [keshurei] - beams of the old synagogue; they needed to place them in the new [one]:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:3:2.english: That which Rav Chisda said - [is stated] in [Tractate] Bava Batra, in [the chapter entitled] HaShutafin:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:3:3.english: Due to negligence - Lest he be negligent and despair, and not build another [synagogue]:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:3:4.english: [In] a case like this, what [is the law] - since its demolition is only for the building of this [new synagogue]:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:4:1.hebrew: חלופי וזבוני - חלה קדושתו על החילוף או על הדמים, והוא יצא מן הקדושה להשתמש בו:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:4:1.english: Exchanging and selling - Its sanctity takes effect upon the exchanged [property] or upon the proceeds, and it [the synagogue] leaves [its] sanctity, [permitting one] to make use of it.

Rashi on Megillah 26b:5:2.english: With old [bricks] - that were already built into the wall of a synagogue that fell:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:5:3.hebrew: אבל בחדתא - שנעשה לשם בית הכנסת, לית לן בה:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:5:3.english: But with new [bricks] - that were made for the sake of a synagogue, we have no [problem] with it:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:6:1.hebrew: ואפי' למ"ד - במסכת סנהדרין בפרק נגמר הדין (סנהדרין דף מז:), גבי אורג בגד למת, דאסור בהזמנה בתכריכי המת, דאסירי בהנאה, דגמרינן "שם" "שם" מעגלה ערופה, כדמפרש התם:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:6:1.english: And even according to the one who said - [This refers to what is discussed] in Tractate Sanhedrin, in the chapter [entitled] Nigmar HaDin (Sanhedrin 47b), regarding one who weaves a garment for a corpse — that it becomes forbidden through [mere] designation as burial shrouds for the deceased, which are forbidden for benefit, as we derive [via a verbal analogy between] "there" [and] "there" from the decapitated calf, as it explains there:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:6:2.hebrew: הני מילי באורג בגד למת - שאינו חסר אלא אריגה, וכיון שנארג, מיד הויא ראוי לפורשו על המת, אבל לבינים מחוסרים עשייה לבנותן בכותל, והלכך בשל לבינים דבית הכנסת הוה ליה כטווי לאריג, וליכא למ"ד בכי האי גוונא דהזמנה מילתא היא:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:6:2.english: This applies [only] to one who weaves a garment for a corpse - for it lacks nothing except weaving, and once it is woven, it is immediately fit to be spread over the corpse; whereas bricks [still] lack [further] work, [namely] to build them into a wall, and therefore in the case of bricks for a synagogue, it is comparable to spun [thread intended] for weaving, and there is no one who says in such a case that designation is significant:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:7:1.english: A gift - [If] the townspeople gave a synagogue [as a gift] for mundane uses:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:8:1.english: And articles of a mitzva - things with which a mitzva was performed:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:8:2.english: Deluskemei [cases] - Like a pouch or a sack in which to place a [scroll]:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:8:3.hebrew: תיק ונרתיק - חדא היא, אלא שלשון "תיק" נופל על דבר ארוך, ולשון "נרתיק" נופל על דבר קצר:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:8:3.english: A container [tik] and a cover [nartik] - [They] are one [and the same], except that the term tik is used for a long object, and the term nartik is used for a short object:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:9:2.hebrew: תשמיש דתשמיש - שפורס מפה עליו, ואחר כך נותן ספר תורה עליו:
Rashi on Megillah 26b:9:2.english: An article of an article - [meaning] that one spreads a cloth upon it, and afterward places a Torah scroll upon it:

Rashi on Megillah 26b:9:3.english: That they place a Torah scroll upon it - without a cloth:

Tosafot on Megillah 26b:10:1.hebrew: מריש הוה אמינא האי פריסא תשמיש דתשמיש הוא - פי' הקונטרס: יריעה שפורסין סביב הארון בתוכו. וקשה, שהרי הארון עצמו הוי תשמיש קדושה, ואמר (התם) שאסור לעשות ממנו כורסיא; אלמא שהתיבה קדושה יותר מן הפורסין. לכך נראה לי שפורסין אותה סביב הארון מבחוץ:
Tosafot on Megillah 26b:10:1.english: Initially, I used to say [that] this curtain is an article of an article [of sanctity] - Rashi explained: [it is] a curtain that they spread around the ark on its inside. And [this] is difficult, for the ark itself is an article of sanctity, as [the Gemara] says (there) that it is forbidden to make a chair from it; thus [it is evident] that the ark is holier than the curtains. Therefore, it appears to me that they spread it around the ark on the outside:

Tosafot on Megillah 26b:4:1.hebrew: אוגורה ומשכונה אסור - קשה, דהא רבי מאיר לא אסר במתניתין אלא ממכר עולם, אבל על תנאי שרי, ומאי שנא? ונראה לי, דהאי דר"מ שרי למכור על תנאי, היינו של רבים לרבים להתפלל שם, דאין במכר זה זלזול; והא דאסרי' הכא משכנתא, הוי דיחיד, משום זלזול:
Tosafot on Megillah 26b:4:1.english: Renting it out or mortgaging it is prohibited - This is difficult, for Rabbi Meir in our Mishnah only prohibited a permanent sale, whereas [a sale] on condition is permitted; so what is the difference? And it seems to me that that which Rabbi Meir permits selling on condition refers to [a sale] from the public to the public to pray there, for in such a sale there is no disrespect; whereas that which we prohibit here [regarding] a mortgage is [a mortgage] to an individual, [which is prohibited] due to disrespect:

Tosafot on Megillah 26b:8:1.hebrew: תשמישי קדושה וכו' נרתק של תפילין ורצועותיהן - מכאן משמע שהדל"ת והיו"ד שבקשר הרצועה אינן אותיות גמורות, ולא הוי הלכה למשה מסיני כי אם השי"ן שבבתים, מדלא קרי הכא לרצועות אלא תשמישי קדושה. והכי נמי משמע בהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף לה: ושם), דלא קרי להו אלא תשמישי קדושה. והכי נמי משמע בפרק שני דשבת (דף כח:), דפריך: "והאמר אביי: שי"ן של תפילין הלכה למשה מסיני", ולא פריך כך מן הדל"ת והיו"ד. ולא קשה מההיא דמנחות (דף לה:), גבי "וראו כל עמי הארץ כי שם ה' נקרא עליך ויראו ממך", ואמרו: "אלו תפילין שבראש" — שיש לפרש הטעם לפי שהן לעולם בגובה של ראש ונראים לעולם שפיר אות, אבל אותן של יד אינן נראין ואין בהן אות, כדכתיב: "והיו לך לאות", ודרשינן (מנחות דף לז:): "ולא לאחרים לאות". אבל למה שפרש"י התם, דהטעם הוי משום שיש בהן השי"ן והדל"ת דהוי רוב אותיות של שדי — לפירוש זה קשה, כדמשמע בכל הני שהבאתי דהיו"ד והדל"ת לא חשיבי אותיות:
Tosafot on Megillah 26b:8:1.english: Articles of sanctity, etc., a cover for phylacteries and their straps - From here it is implied that the dalet and the yod that are in the knot of the strap are not full-fledged letters, and [only] the shin on the [phylactery] boxes is a law [given] to Moses at Sinai, since here [the baraita] calls the straps nothing other than "articles of sanctity." And so too it is implied in [the chapter] Hakometz Rabbah (Menachot 35b, and there), where it calls them nothing other than "articles of sanctity." And so too it is implied in the second chapter of Shabbat (28b), where [the Gemara] raises an objection: "But did not Abaye say: The shin of phylacteries is a law [given] to Moses at Sinai?" — and it does not raise such an objection from the dalet and the yod. And there is no difficulty from that [teaching] in Menachot (35b), regarding [the verse], "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you," [concerning which] they said: "These are the phylacteries on the head" — for one can explain the reason [is] because they are always on the height of the head and are always clearly visible [as] a sign, whereas those of the hand are not visible and do not have [the status of] a sign, as it is written: "And it shall be to you for a sign," and we expound (Menachot 37b): "[To you,] and not to others for a sign." However, according to what Rashi explained there, that the reason is because they have the shin and the dalet, which constitute the majority of the letters of Shaddai — according to this explanation it is difficult, as is implied in all these [passages] that I have cited, that the yod and the dalet are not considered letters:
